doc.title: Mike Longo interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 13, 2019

title: Studying with Oscar Peterson and the Art Tatum thumb story
summary: Through Jimmy McPartland in Chicago he met Oscar Peterson, studied six months in Toronto, and Rowe and Longo trade Tatum stories.

story.theme_name: Pianists: who played, who influenced whom
story.community_name: Art Tatum: the legend, the piano and the man

blocks.x: used to be a place across the street called the Copper Rail. It was a soul food place. And all those old guys from the old school jazz, they were all drinkers. “Have a drink, have a drink.” By the time it was 8:00 I was out of it. And the bar tender would be sending me up pieces of Italian bread to soak up, so I could play the gig. But I was learning a lot. And then I got to — I went to Chicago with Jimmy McPartland. And I met this boxer, Connie Milano. And he said he was a friend of Oscar Peterson’s and that Oscar was playing at the London House. He said, “I want to take you over to meet Oscar.” So I met Oscar. He said, “Why don’t you come by my hotel tomorrow and play for me, I want to talk to you about something.” So I had a little Wurlitzer electric piano and I played it. He said, “How’d you like to study with me?” I said, “Are you kidding?” So apparently he had this school in Toronto. They had the Advanced School of Contemporary Music. So I made arrangements and went up there and studied six months with him, and that totally changed my life. Like the first lesson I had with him I said man, I can’t play. I listened to him play I said, “What?” So he had me practicing 13 hours a day.
But he said the same thing, sort of, at least in a story I heard, that when he heard Art Tatum he said, “Man I can’t play.” So it’s all relative.

Man he had this funny story. He said Art, on this recording was playing this run and he was driving himself nuts trying to figure it out. So when Art got in town he sat ringside, right next to the piano, till he played that run. He said he was dragging his thumb. Playing notes and dragging his thumb. And he said Oscar was actually trying to play that and he was saying it’s not on the piano. You know? He said he was dragging his thumb. But he was pianistically influenced by Art but musically he was more influenced by Dizzy. He said Dizzy was his main influence.
